newsitem.title: UK: British family doctor arrested after patient death.
newsitem.headline: British family doctor arrested after patient death.

text.p: A British family doctor embroiled in a euthanasia controversy has been arrested following the death of an 85-year old patient, a police spokeswoman said on Wednesday.
The police said no charges have been brought against Dr Dave Moor, who was being held for questioning.
Moor was arrested early on Wednesday after arriving voluntarily at a police station in Newcastle, in northeast England.
"Dr Moor has been arrested and is being questioned. He came in by prior arrangement with his solicitors (lawyers). So far no charges have been brought," the police spokeswoman said.
He faces questioning about the death of former ambulanceman George Liddell, she said.
The funeral of Liddell, a cancer victim who had been treated by Moor, was halted by a Newcastle coroner last week ahead of a police investigation.
British health chiefs started their own inquiry eight days ago into whether Moor should face criminal prosecution after the doctor admitted he had helped 150 people to die during his 30-year career.

While doctors can administer drugs to help relieve patients' pain, British law bars them from carrying out mercy killings or from helping dying patients to kill themselves. There have been growing calls in Britain for the legalisation of euthanasia.
